rounds.response: Thank you — we appreciate you putting a full package on the table, but as presented it is unacceptable to our members. The proposed 2.5/2/2 wage pattern and any increase in employee health premiums will be rejected; we come back with a counter of 6% in year one and 4% in each of years two and three, with no increase in employee health premium contributions. We also reject the requested weekend-scheduling concessions unless any additional weekend work is strictly voluntary, paid at a meaningful premium, limited in frequency, and preserves current advance-notice protections. If you expect us to consider tradeoffs, provide the underlying financial and health-plan data (premium trends, utilization, and your modeling) so we can evaluate your sustainability claims. We’re prepared to bargain in good faith, but we need a materially improved economic offer and firm protections on scheduling before we can move forward.
